item.title: Was DeMarvion Overshown penalty an indictment of Dallas Cowboys discipline and team culture
item.description: Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (0) penalty against the Indianapolis Colts las week week was an indictment of the team's discipline and culture. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images To know Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is to know that his heart is always in the right place. His worth ethic, his dedication to the team and his faith can’t be questioned. Neither can his ability to overcome setbacks and hardships, considering he has missed 38 games due to injuries since his rookie season in 2023. So his embarrassing penalty in the 33-30 victory against the Indianapolis Colts last week can be initially brushed off as an overexcited indiscretion of youthful exuberance on his part. He came onto the field to celebrate after Quinnen Williams forced a Jonathan Taylor fumble that Shemar James returned to the Dallas 30. Overshown was penalized 15 yards, with referee Clay Martin saying, “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We have non-uniformed player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That’s a 15-yard penalty.” The ref got specific about the outfit pic.twitter.com/NpJc5qdgBA — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 8, 2026 He was just trying to celebrate with his beaten down defensive teammates after a big play. That he ran on the field in street clothes because he was inactive for the game with an injury is where it crossed the line. Overshown, who apologized to his teammates afterwards, said don’t blame coach Brian Schottenheimer, blame him. It is fault alone. “At the end of the day, I talked to Schotty about it,” Overshown said. “I apologized about it. It was definitely in the moment, but earlier I had said that as a defense, we’re going to start celebrating more, getting takeaways. And I was just caught in the moment. So you can laugh at it now, because we won the game, but in the moment, fourth quarter, tied ball game or close ball game, you don’t want a 15-yard penalty from a guy, especially that’s not even playing. So that’s a lesson learned.” “It’s not an indictment on Schotty. It’s on me as a player. I own it,” he said. The problem is that in taking ownership of penalty he unwittingly indicted Schottenheimer and the Cowboys coaching staff. Overshown said he didn’t know he could run on the field if he wasn’t in uniform until veteran linebacker Dee Winters told him. “Honestly, I really didn’t know the rules,” Overshown said. “I was running on the field and (Dee Winters) was like, ‘D-Mo you can’t be out here.’ And that’s when I looked back and I had already seen the ref pointing at me. item.title: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente provides positive update on Lamine Yamal’s fitness: ‘In perfect condition’
item.description: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente provides positive update on Lamine Yamal’s fitness: ‘In perfect condition’ Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal is expected to return to Spain’s squad for Sunday’s UEFA Nations League meeting with England after recovering from a knee problem that ruled him out of the 2-0 victory over the Czech Republic. Spain coach Luis de la Fuente confirmed that the 19-year-old was feeling much better and would rejoin the national team ahead of the decisive Group A3 encounter at the Metropolitano. The announcement provides a timely boost for Spain, who have already secured their place in the quarter-finals but still need to protect their position at the top of the group. Barcelona and Spain medical teams prioritise Yamal’s recovery Yamal remained in Barcelona after experiencing discomfort in his right knee during the 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on November 8. An MRI scan detected inflammation and fluid in the joint, prompting both medical departments to agree that he should receive treatment at his club rather than travel to Prague. Lamine Yamal did not play against Czech Republic. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Speaking after Spain’s victory against the Czech Republic, De la Fuente offered an encouraging update. “The truth is, we have good news. Lamine Yamal is feeling much better and is eager to join the training camp tomorrow. Mikel [Oyarzabal] is too. “One will arrive around midday and the other a little later, but both will be with us tomorrow. “Lamine is in perfect condition and ready to play full 90 minutes,” he confirmed, as per SPORT . De la Fuente responds to questions about special treatment Yamal’s absence and delayed arrival generated discussion about whether the Barcelona youngster was receiving preferential treatment from the national team. De la Fuente confirms Lamine Yamal will play against England. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) De la Fuente had previously rejected those suggestions , insisting that the decision was based entirely on medical considerations, stating, “Lamine has no privileges.” In fact, the Spaniard had previously explained that he consulted Barcelona’s medical staff before deciding against making the forward travel to Prague. Meanwhile, Spain will face England on Sunday, November 15, with the Group A3 leadership at stake. De la Fuente’s side have collected 15 points from five matches, while England sit three points behind after beating Croatia 2-1. Notably, both nations have qualified for the quarter-finals, meaning the result will determine their final group positions and not qualification.

item.title: Real Madrid star admits he would have preferred Mbappe or Yamal to win Ballon d’Or over Harry Kane
item.description: Real Madrid star admits he would have preferred Mbappe or Yamal to win Ballon d’Or over Harry Kane Real Madrid made a number of star signings in the summer, including Marc Cucurella from Chelsea. The Spaniard’s arrival gave Los Blancos a World Cup winner in their squad. He took some time to settle into life at Madrid but has slowly come into his own in recent weeks. Cucurella has now spoken about the 2026 Ballon d’Or, which continues to generate debate weeks after Harry Kane was crowned the winner. Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe narrowly finished behind the Englishman, missing out by just 28 points. Speaking to El Chiringuito TV , Cucurella explained why Mbappe or Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal would have been his preferred choice. Cucurella surprised by Kane’s Ballon d’Or victory Asked whether Kane’s triumph was unfair, Cucurella acknowledged the extraordinary numbers the Englishman produced last season. Kylian Mbappe deserved the 2026 Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) “Not unfair, because he reached numbers that he probably won’t reach again,” the Madrid defender explained (h/t Madrid Xtra ). However, the Spaniard admitted that he would have preferred one of his club or national team-mates to win the award. “But for me, I’d have given it to Kylian Mbappe or Lamine because personally as a fan, I’d turn on the TV to watch them play,” he explained. “It’s not that Kane didn’t deserve it, but it did surprise me,” Cucurella added. Mbappe came agonisingly close Kylian Mbappe enjoyed a dream individual season, performing at an astonishing level for both Los Blancos and the France national team at the World Cup. The voting results revealed just how narrowly Mbappe missed out on his first Ballon d’Or. Kane received 1,055 points compared to Mbappe’s 1,027. Mbappe came very close to pipping Harry Kane to the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The Englishman scored an extraordinary 73 goals for club and country last season, helping Bayern secure a domestic treble. Ultimately, those numbers seemed too good for most journalists to overlook, helping the Bayern star win the award. However, Cucurella is right to believe that Mbappe deserved the award . The Frenchman performed when the lights shone brightest. Had he added at least one piece of silverware to his cabinet, there is no doubt that the Frenchman would have walked away with the award. Mbappe has started this season in exceptional fashion once again, and it remains to be seen whether he can do enough to go one step further next year.

item.title: Liverpool and Van Dijk have a decision to make
item.description: Virgil van Dijk joined Liverpool for £75m from Southampton in January 2018 [Getty Images] After Liverpool beat Brighton in October, Virgil van Dijk went upstairs to the Boardroom at Anfield and met up with Alan Hansen. It was Van Dijk who, at the end of the 2024-25 season, asked the former Liverpool and Scotland defender to present him with the Premier League trophy and this time they posed for a picture that inevitably did the rounds on social media. Whenever the time comes for Van Dijk to move on from Liverpool, he will go down as arguably their greatest centre-half, alongside Hansen. The question now is whether he will finish his career at Anfield like Hansen did in 1991. Van Dijk's contract expires next summer and, even if the 35-year-old insisted this week that he was in no panic, it is a topic that will be a source of debate until a decision is made. "Let's see what the season brings. I've had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that's the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else," the Liverpool captain told reporters at Selhurst Park. Two seasons ago, with Van Dijk in a similar situation, there was a similar sense of calm and come April 2025 he signed a two-year-deal. Judging by Van Dijk's comments there is a feeling of him wanting to stay, but both he and Liverpool have an important decision to make. Van Dijk and Alan Hansen are regarded as two of Liverpool's greatest defenders [@VirgilVanDijk] Liverpool keen to avoid Salah repeat Aside from a poor error against Villarreal in the Champions League, Van Dijk has shown this season that his standards haven't dropped. His partnership with Jeremy Jacquet, who joined in the summer, is going from strength to strength and Van Dijk has played every minute in the Premier League since the start of last season. A "little niggle" has affected him in recent weeks and this is the first international window he has missed with the Netherlands since Euro 2020, but it isn't a major cause for concern. Liverpool have lost a number of senior figures in recent years but Van Dijk remains a leader in every form, and that was evidenced by his suggestion to Andoni Iraola that the squad should visit the museum at Anfield to learn more about the club's history. At Crystal Palace on Sunday, it spoke volumes of Van Dijk's character that he came over to a group of reporters and asked if they wanted to speak to him, rather than the other way around. He regularly fronts up, regardless of the result. Van Dijk is certainly not the force he was under Jurgen Klopp but he remains an elite centre-half and the stats justify that. item.title: Ten-man Betis survive Navalcarnero scare at Santo Domingo as Riquelme wins it in extra time
item.description: Ten-man Betis survive Navalcarnero scare at Santo Domingo as Riquelme wins it in extra time Real Betis needed a stoppage-time equaliser and extra time to beat Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey round of 128. Manuel Pellegrini's weakened side avoided an upset and now await the second-round draw. Real Betis came from behind late on to beat Navalcarnero in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Thursday 12 November. Riquelme settled the tie in extra time at Santo Domingo. Manuel Pellegrini’s side finished with ten men after Aitor Ruibal was sent off. The venue carried history for the Betis coach. Santo Domingo is where Pellegrini, then in charge of Real Madrid, suffered the 2009 cup defeat known as the ‘Alcorconazo’, El Gol Digital noted. Navalcarnero, founded in 1953, play in Group V of Segunda Federación. The club moved the tie away from its own Municipal Mariano González ground. It chose Santo Domingo, which holds roughly 5,000, to make room for its more than 2,000 members. The club said money was not the only reason. Betis trailed late on before Riquelme’s extra-time winner Riquelme opened the scoring in the fifth minute from a Ruibal assist, and Betis led at half-time. Álvaro Leis equalised in the 49th minute from a free-kick routine set up by Navalcarnero’s coach. Leis then turned provider for K. Vazquez, who put the hosts ahead in the 79th minute. Marina levelled in stoppage time, with Ruibal credited with the assist. Riquelme’s second goal came in the 96th minute. Diego Llorente went off in extra time after a heavy blow to the head. Isco missed a penalty in the 117th minute. Already booked in the 90+4th minute, Ruibal received a second yellow and a red card in the 118th. Navalcarnero felt they should have had a penalty for a challenge by Pablo Fornals, and the tie was played without VAR, Infobae (EFE) reported. The figures show how much Betis dominated. They had 73% of the ball, took 29 shots to Navalcarnero’s 12 and won 13 corners to 3. They completed 864 accurate passes. Dani Ceballos earned a 9.2 rating with 3 key passes. On the same night, Levante also needed extra time in the first round, winning 2-1 away to CD Tarancón. A depleted Betis squad now turns to the derby and the draw Betis were without several regulars. Valles, Marc Roca, Abde, Parrott, Deossa and four other players were away on international duty. Cucho Hernández was injured. Betis agreed the new date after talks with the RFEF and Navalcarnero, knowing that any players called up by their national teams would miss the match. The win follows a 2-0 victory over Elche. For Navalcarnero, the defeat ended a run of five matches without loss, including a 3-2 win over Numancia. They host Getafe II in Segunda División RFEF on Sunday 15 November. item.title: Revealed: Roma rejected €60mln plus Gittens for Kone
item.description: Revealed: Roma rejected €60mln plus Gittens for Kone Chelsea were ready to offer around €60 million plus the loan of Jamie Gittens, the very winger Roma were desperately seeking. But Gian Piero Gasperini wouldn’t listen: Manu Koné had to stay at Trigoria. This wall was erected on the final day of the summer transfer window, and, in light of what happened in the following months, it speaks volumes about the French midfielder’s importance to the team’s stability. This behind the scenes look is revealed today by Il Messaggero , which emphasizes how the relationship between Koné and Gasperini wasn’t always easy, especially towards the end of last season. Now, however, the situation has changed. The Frenchman has become one of Roma’s key players, especially for his ability to protect the defense, win back possession, and quickly transform defensive play into attack. The numbers confirm this. Returning to the starting lineup against Sassuolo after a three-week layoff with a muscle injury, Koné completed all 56 attempted passes, winning five of six duels and recovering three balls. It was a solid performance, which restored Gasperini’s role as a key player in midfield.

item.title: ‘The one guy’: Tim Hardaway Sr. says Luka Doncic could now do something that hasn’t happened in 64 years
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images Luka Doncic has had an incredible start to the new season. The Los Angeles Lakers superstar has averaged 38.6 points per game so far and is leading the race to win the MVP award at the end of the campaign. Doncic has already broken a few records this season, but Tim Hardaway Sr. believes he could match one of the biggest achievements in NBA history. Tim Hardaway Sr. says Luka Doncic could score 100 points in a game Scoring 50 points in a game is an extraordinary achievement, and Doncic has managed to do it twice already this season – 53 against the Trail Blazers and 52 against the Jazz. The Slovenian’s highest tally in a single game came when he was with the Dallas Mavericks. He scored 73 points against the Hawks in January 2024. Doncic’s best single-game record for the Lakers is 60 points. It came in March this year against the Miami Heat. Yet, Hardaway Sr. believes the Los Angeles superstar is the only player in the entire NBA right now capable of scoring 100 points in a single game. He said on the Run It Back show : “That Luka man, he’s a phenomenal player. One-on-one, right now, nobody can stop him. “I always say this, if he gets on a roll and he wants to score 100, that’s the one guy who can do it. That’s the one guy who can score a 100 if he gets on a roll.” Only one player in the history of the NBA has managed to score 100 points in a single game. That was Wilt Chamberlain for the Philadelphia Warriors in a 169–147 victory over the New York Knicks all the way back in 1962 – 64 years ago! Doncic has never even come close to matching that record, but if he proves Hardaway Sr. right and scores a century, it could become the biggest achievement in modern basketball. item.title: 'A lie' & 'nonsense' - Palmer committed to England, says Rogers
item.description: Cole Palmer and Morgan are Chelsea team-mates [Getty Images] Morgan Rogers says any suggestion Cole Palmer is not committed to England "is a lie" and "nonsense". Rogers scored the opener in Wednesday's 2-1 Uefa Nations League win over Croatia , with Harry Kane adding a penalty on his record-breaking 126th appearance for the men's side. But his Chelsea team-mate, and childhood friend, Palmer had been left out of the squad after boss Thomas Tuchel said he "misses too many chances to impress". The 24-year-old Palmer, who was also not called up for the World Cup, withdrew from the previous England camp in September citing a minor injury. Forward Rogers, also 24, was asked about the criticism of Palmer following the win at Wembley, and told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He wants to be here. "He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. "He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. "But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it. "It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. It's a lie. "You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it." Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel? A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma History for Kane but what would England do without him? Struggles under Tuchel In the three years since his England debut, Palmer has only won 14 caps, scoring two goals - including one in the Euro 2024 final defeat by Spain - and having one assist. That is despite scoring 50 Premier League goals with 24 assists. He was named England's men's player of the year for the 2023-24 season after some impressive form, including his strike against Spain in the Berlin showpiece. But Palmer has only featured in three of Tuchel's 27 games since he succeeded Gareth Southgate as manager. Some sketchy form last season, though, meant the former Manchester City player missed out on the the summer World Cup, with England going on to finish third after losing to Argentina in the semi-final. He was named in Tuchel's first squad after that, but withdrew despite having played in all Chelsea's league games to that point. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Football club backs men's mental health initiative
item.description: Colin Eley said the club and foundation wanted to give something back to the fans [Nottingham Forest Foundation] Mental health support is reaching football fans where they gather most. An initiative has been launched in the safe standing section of the lower John Robertson Stand at Nottingham Forest's City Ground to encourage supporters to open up about their mental health. A QR code in the stand provides access to mental health charity Say It Lad's website, where visitors can listen to anonymous voice notes shared by men talking openly about their own experiences and can also record their own. Colin Eley, health and wellbeing manager at Nottingham Forest Foundation, said the main goal was to make sure people "don't feel alone in going through any kind of mental health challenges". The QR codes can be found on stickers in the safe standing section of the lower John Robertson Stand [Nottingham Forest Foundation] Jonny Human, Say It Lad's founder and creative lead, said: "We don't respond to every voice note, that's not the idea of our platform, but every voice note does get heard. "So if you have got something that you want to say and that you want to share, then we will listen. "Someone will listen to your voice note and they will take it on board. So you're not just speaking into a void." Jonny Human said the initiative came from his own struggles with mental health [Nottingham Forest Foundation] The organisation has worked with football clubs across the country, including Southampton, Southend United and Ipswich Town. Jonny said his desire to help others came from his own struggles with mental health. "I thought 'well I need to stop any other lad getting to that point and I need to have a platform there to let people know about what to expect'." Icons including David Beckham and Megan Rapinoe lead the latest class of inductees to the National Soccer Hall of Fame. These legendary figures will be celebrated for their massive impact on both the international stage and the growth of the domestic game. Hall of Fame welcomes football icons Former USWNT stars Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have been elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame, alongside ex-USMNT striker Jozy Altidore. Rapinoe claimed two World Cups and a Ballon d'Or during a glittering career, while Ertz firmly established herself as one of the world's premier defensive midfielders. Meanwhile, Altidore ranks third in US men's history with 42 international goals. David Beckham also earned his place via the veteran ballot. The former England captain sparked immense growth in the American game after joining LA Galaxy in 2007, where he won consecutive league titles. He later returned as an owner to launch Inter Miami. Brazilian indoor football specialist Tatu and former USMNT coach Lothar Osiander were also voted in to complete the historic class. 'A part of great teams' Rapinoe, who earned election on her first year of eligibility, received the news during a surprise celebration involving family and supporters at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The Seattle Reign icon expressed deep gratitude for the recognition alongside her peers. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my teammates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe shared in a video posted to Instagram . "So, I definitely was a part of some great teams, and yeah, it's very special." Beckham's American legacy cemented Beckham learned of his induction directly from MLS commissioner Don Garber during a league board meeting. Garber praised the Manchester United legend's transformational impact on the sport across the Atlantic. "The National Soccer Hall of Fame recognises the players and builders who have profoundly shaped the sport," Garber said when delivering the news. "It is my honour to welcome you to the National Soccer Hall of Fame. Congratulations David." "This has been an incredible journey. I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this country for a long time. So thank you," Beckham responded. Texas ceremony awaits The distinguished group will be officially enshrined into the Hall of Fame on April 16 next year in Plano, Texas. The spring ceremony will celebrate a diverse class that fundamentally reshaped football in the United States, honouring both international dominance and domestic league expansion. item.description: Thierno Barry is becoming more of a household name every single week now as he continues to bang in the goals for Everton . Barry was a name plastered all over social media in the opening few weeks of the season, mainly due to the number of chances he was missing. In more recent weeks, Barry has been all over the media for more positive reasons, as he starts to turn his missed chances into goals. It's something we've spoken about on the channel multiple times this season , suggesting that Barry missing chances is a positive overall. It was always going to start levelling out, and even now, we could still see Barry on more goals. The French striker is now on six goals in the Premier League, while he's contributed 13 goals and assists in 13 games in all competitions. Barry is slowly starting to get the respect he deserves , and that will only continue if he keeps putting the ball in the back of the net. At the end of the day, strikers will be judged on how many times they score goals, especially by casual football fans who aren't watching Everton as religiously as us. David Moyes has certainly been impressed with Barry in recent weeks, and hopefully that will continue long into the season. Barry is now becoming a topic of discussion among football podcasts, with many starting to take notice of the towering striker. item.title: Bayern Munich determined to do everything possible to renew Real Madrid target’s contract – Romano
item.description: Bayern Munich determined to do everything possible to renew Real Madrid target’s contract – Romano Yan Diomande has settled well into his role at Real Madrid, to the point where he appears set to take over as an undisputed starter. Jose Mourinho, however, will face a dilemma after the break. With Vinicius Jr. set to return to action after the international hiatus, the manager must decide if he retains Diomande on the left wing or continues to back the Brazilian on the left with Diomande on the right wing. Given how Vinicius’ saga is unfolding, it is not ruled out that he leaves the club soon, and Real Madrid already have one name in mind as a more effective solution to the wings – Michael Olise. While there are no direct connections between the club’s pursuit of him and Vinicius’ departure, that would appear to be a logical step forward. Real Madrid still eyeing Olise Olise wanted to join Real Madrid. (Photo by Pauline Figuet/Getty Images) In a recent update, the ever-reliable Fabrizio Romano confirmed Real Madrid’s interest in Olise and backed the reports from earlier this week . For starters, the Italian journalist stated that Bayern Munich are working very hard to secure the Frenchman’s renewal and that they are directing all their efforts towards the same. The Germans will offer a top contract, not only in a financial but also in a sporting sense, to convince the player to stay. Real Madrid, for their part, continue to monitor Olise’s situation closely, and the journalist adds that Los Blancos’ administrators, including Florentino Perez, ‘love’ the player. The story of last summer Real Madrid remain alert. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) It is common knowledge at this point that Real Madrid were desperate to sign Olise last summer, and that even the player was keen on the switch to Spain. Romano now brings to light that the reason the club did not send an offer to Germany was to preserve their relations with Bayern Munich. If not for that nuance, Real Madrid would have sent an official offer letter for the player who even wanted the move deeply. Should Olise not renew his deal now and push for a change in scenery, Bayern will have no option but to open the doors to negotiations – something Real Madrid are desperately waiting for. What is clear, however, is that Yan Diomande’s arrival does not rule out Olise’s signing in any sense.

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino will revive Man United by making Bruno Fernandes the fulcrum of his system
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino will revive Man United by making Bruno Fernandes the fulcrum of his system Manchester United have already announced the departure of manager Michael Carrick after a disappointing start to the new season. The Red Devils are languishing in 18th place in the Premier League after 10 games, with just one win to their name. Recent reports suggest INEOS have already reached an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to take over at Old Trafford. The Argentine manager is currently in charge of the USMNT and is likely to arrive at the Theatre of Dreams at the end of the international break. Meanwhile, Carrick’s struggles have been baffling since he managed to secure third place in the league with the same set of players last season. Bruno Fernandes had been on fire under the English manager last campaign, managing four goals and 14 assists in 17 appearances. item.title: Why Messi Is Favored to Win a Third Straight MLS MVP
item.description: Why Messi Is Favored to Win a Third Straight MLS MVP Lionel Messi finished the 2026 MLS regular season with 26 goals and 17 assists, becoming the first player in league history to win back-to-back Golden Boots. Finalists for the Landon Donovan MVP award are being revealed this week, and Messi enters as the heavy favorite to win a third straight trophy — something no player in MLS history has done. What happened: the numbers behind the favorite tag Messi's 2026 regular season closed with a league-high 43 goal contributions , finishing four goals clear of FC Dallas striker Petar Musa and five ahead of Nashville's Sam Surridge in the scoring race. He also notched 17 assists, trailing only Charlotte's Pep Biel for the league lead in that category. Inter Miami, meanwhile, finished third in the Eastern Conference — well short of the Supporters' Shield, which Nashville SC claimed with a league-record points total. Why the gap between team and individual results doesn't hurt his case MLS MVP voting splits evenly between club technical staff, players and media, and the award has historically tracked individual output more closely than team silverware. That pattern favors Messi again this year. Carlos Vela won MVP in 2019 without a Shield or Cup, and Messi's own 2025 MVP arrived on a Miami team that finished third in the East before a late playoff run to the title. Surridge and Hany Mukhtar can point to Nashville's historic points tally, and Brian White has a strong goals-per-90 case for Vancouver. But no challenger matches Messi's combination of scoring volume, chance creation and MLS's own metric of goal contributions, the stat the league has repeatedly used to frame the MVP conversation. Mukhtar and Surridge's campaigns strengthen the ballot field without changing the top line: Messi led the league in total output for a second consecutive year, this time at age 39 and in a season that also included Argentina's run to the World Cup final. What it means: history, workload and the road to 2028 A third MVP would make Messi the only player in MLS history to win the award in three separate seasons, pulling clear of Preki, the only other two-time winner. It would also extend a run that began in his first full season with Miami in 2024 and has continued through a World Cup cycle without any visible drop in production — a workload data point clubs across the league will track as Messi's contract runs through 2028. For MLS, the significance is less about the trophy and more about continuity. A third straight MVP keeps the league's most marketable storyline — Messi outproducing a league that has grown around him — intact heading into a 2027 season where expansion, new rivals and a deeper Golden Boot field will eventually test whether this run has a ceiling.

item.title: Barcelona could benefit as former defender attracts interest from top European clubs
item.description: Barcelona could benefit as former defender attracts interest from top European clubs Barcelona could benefit further from Alvaro Cortes’ departure to Royal Antwerp, as the young defender attracts attention from several major European clubs after an encouraging start in Belgium. According to SPORT , the centre-back’s performances have caught the eye of potential suitors, giving the Catalan club a strong reason to monitor his development after negotiating a transfer that protects its financial interests. The 21-year-old academy star left Barcelona in September 2026 after the two clubs reached an agreement for his permanent transfer. Although the move ended his five-year spell in Catalonia, the terms allow Barça to retain a financial stake in his future. Cortes has established himself at Royal Antwerp Cortes has wasted little time establishing himself in Belgium. Rather than spending his initial months adapting from the sidelines, the Spanish centre-back has become a regular presence in Antwerp’s defensive line. His involvement is reflected in his early league record, as Cortes has made seven Belgian First Division A appearances, completing 630 minutes. He started every one of those matches, which shows the responsibility he has received since arriving from Barcelona. Having captained Barça Atlètic during the 2025/26 campaign, Cortes needed a pathway towards senior football, and he got that through Antwerp. Barcelona retained financial protection after his departure Notably, Barcelona did not allow Cortes to leave without securing future benefits. Alvaro Cortes has made a strong impact at Royal Antwerp. (Picture credit: X/@official_rafc) The agreement was worth €3.5 million, with the Catalan club also retaining a percentage of a subsequent transfer. Reports have also mentioned a buy-back arrangement, although the club’s official announcement did not disclose such a clause. Now, the interest is significant because Cortes offers a profile that fits Barcelona’s traditional preference for defenders comfortable in possession. His left-footed distribution and ability to find vertical passing lanes could become valuable assets as his experience grows. However, interest from bigger clubs does not automatically translate into a transfer, and his progress must be judged over a longer period. Barcelona, on their part, are in a win-win situation. If he indeed have a buy-back clause, they will hope the defender excels, and if external interest grows, they will benefit financially.

Had the Londoners had it their way, it would've been Khadija Shaw's first game against her old side. Chelsea's pursuit of Shaw last season was no secret. Catarina Macario's move to the San Diego Wave , Sam Kerr's looming exit and Mayra Ramirez's injury issues made signing a centre-forward a major priority in the summer window for the Blues. So, with contract talks between Shaw and City stalling, Chelsea were ready to pounce to secure the signature of one of the best strikers on the planet , if not the best. For a while, it looked like Shaw was nailed on to swap Manchester for west London too, only for it all to change at the last. As City's celebrations surrounding a first WSL title in 10 years commenced, the Jamaica international revealed that she had signed a new four-year deal with the club , giving the champions a huge boost while simultaneously dealing one of their biggest rivals a massive blow. As the two teams prepare to go head-to-head for the first time this season though, it is Chelsea who are the top-scorers in the WSL, even though they sit two points behind City at the top of the table. Some were not convinced by the manner in which the club responded to Shaw's snub, but the early signs have certainly been good - with there potentially even more to come. With top-class centre-forwards so difficult to find, it looked like all of those on the market had slipped through their fingers. And so Chelsea changed tact a little. item.title: Mike Tomlin 'deputized' Joey Porter for Bengals-Steelers playoff fight
item.description: Former Pittsburgh head coach Mike Tomlin shared new information about one of the most memorable moments in the AFC North rivalry between the Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals ahead of their NFL Week 10 showdown on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. Tomlin, now an analyst for NBC Sports, appeared on Steelers defensive lineman Cam Heyward's "Not Just Football" podcast and talked about the infamous playoff incident involving former Pittsburgh linebackers coach Joey Porter Sr. Porter was fined $10,000 for an altercation with Bengals defensive back Adam "Pacman" Jones after Porter went onto the field to check on an injured Antonio Brown following Vontaze Burfict's hit during Pittsburgh's 18-16 AFC Wild Card win against Cincinnati in Jan. 2016. The "Joey Porter rule" in 2016 was one of four changes, clarifications or reminders the NFL established resulting from the Bengals-Steelers rivalry. "I deputized him," Tomlin said on Heyward's podcast . "We had a nasty relationship with that group. And so I called him in my office before that game on game day. I said if it goes berserk, I'm coming on the field. I want you to come with me. I want you to control our guys. When they hit (Brown) and he was asleep, Pouncey and those guys were at the brink. And so I went on the field." "I signaled to him, come on," Tomlin continued. "He went out there as a peacemaker under my direction. And he gets out there and he's operating as peacemaker, but they are pissed that he is on the field. Different people got different talents. And I knew if it got crazy, he was the man for the job." When Porter was featured in the second episode of "Hard Knocks: In Season with the AFC North," he said he refuses to eat in Cincinnati, Baltimore or Cleveland because of how NFL fans in those cities feel about him. NBC Sports analyst Devin McCourty said he's eager to see the reception Sunday night for Tomlin at Paycor Stadium. Tomlin poked fun at the Bengals in September as he and others reviewed highlights from Cincinnati's 30-27 Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. "Former Steeler Ke'Shawn Williams muffs a punt ," Tomlin said on the broadcast during the highlight. "He forgets that he's not playing for them. Another error by their punt return team, giving the Steelers another shot. … All is well in western PA." When Tomlin spoke in Pittsburgh Sept. 25 for the Steelers' Hall of Honor ceremony, he said he wished "he could be here Sunday for this butt-kicking that we gonna put on the Cincinnati Bengals." Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was asked whether it would be weird to be in a production meeting with Tomlin as NBC Sports analyst. "I've always loved how he sees the game and attacks coaching," Burrow told reporters. "He's always attacked it with an intensity that I had a lot of respect for, and so to be able to get to know him in a setting like that, I think, would be a little exciting for me." item.description: Australia captain Pat Cummins has strongly rejected Usman Khawaja's claims that the entire Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper during the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa. Cummins addressed the allegations during a 68-minute press conference at Cricket Central in Sydney. He called Khawaja's claims "100% wrong" and "complete and utter nonsense". Khawaja, in his recently published autobiography, alleged that the entire Australia XI knew about the use of sandpaper in the Cape Town Test. He also claimed that two players had refused to take collective responsibility for the incident. Cummins responded to several allegations, spoke about the 2018 investigation, his relationship with Khawaja, the punishments handed to Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, and his current relationship with Smith. Key points from Pat Cummins' press conference Did the entire Australian team know about the sandpaper? Cummins strongly denied Khawaja's claim that all 11 players knew sandpaper was being used to tamper with the ball during the Cape Town Test in 2018. "When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong," Cummins said. "I've said that consistently for the last eight years, I did not know that was happening. "But I think Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that. "He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball-tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense. I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam [Bancroft] to be careful when using sandpaper. — 7Cricket (@7Cricket) "That's not the Usman that I know. "I support his right to tell a story 100%. I'm really glad that he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do." Was there a master-plan to tamper with the ball? Cummins admitted that the Australian team had a win-at-all-costs mentality in 2018. item.title: ‘This Is Football, Not a Reality TV Drama’ — Browns Fans Take Aim At Veteran Reporter For ‘Creating’ Shedeur Sanders Vs. Deshaun Watson Narrative
item.description: ‘This Is Football, Not a Reality TV Drama’ — Browns Fans Take Aim At Veteran Reporter For ‘Creating’ Shedeur Sanders Vs. Deshaun Watson Narrative The Cleveland Browns settled their Week 10 quarterback question Wednesday morning, naming Deshaun Watson the starter for Sunday’s game against the Houston Texans. However, a question about how they got there has put a Browns beat reporter in some fans’ crosshairs. When Watson met with reporters Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot, who covers the Browns for Cleveland.com, asked whether he knew why head coach Todd Monken had left the door open Monday for Shedeur Sanders to start. Watson’s answer opened with “I have no idea,” and after Cabot posted the clip, some fans turned their questions on her instead. Why Browns Fans Are Mad at Mary Kay Cabot With his Week 8 concussion keeping Watson inactive in New Orleans, Sanders got his first start of the season and nearly stole it, throwing for 297 yards and two touchdowns without an interception before the Browns fell 23-22 in overtime on a failed two-point try. His 72.8 PFN QB Impact Grade for Week 9 ranked 16th in the league, ahead of names like Drake Maye, Jared Goff, Matthew Stafford, and J.J. McCarthy. With that performance still fresh, Monken was asked on his video call Monday, the day after the loss, whether he was ready to name a starter for the Texans game. He answered plainly, “I am not.” Two days later, Watson was the one fielding a question about that Monday answer, and after his opening line, he chose not to speak for his coach. “I’m not sure. You have to ask Monk about that. My job is to just come in every day and whatever’s required for the day is what I do.” One fan wondered whether the people covering the team are even on its side, asking Cabot , “Do y’all even like the team you report on? This is football, not a reality TV drama.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Another fan made the same point more bluntly, wanting to know, “Why would you even ask something like that?” Two more fans looked past the question and went after Cabot’s motives, with one telling her, “It’s lazy and lackluster. You’re into creating narratives, and that’ll get you nowhere.” The other put the question down to a hunt for traffic, saying, “There they go again, stirring the pot. item.description: Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg (32) works around Minnesota Timberwolves guard Jaylen Clark (7) during the second half of an NBA basketball game Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, in Minneapolis. (Matt Krohn/AP Photo/Matt Krohn) MINNEAPOLIS – The Dallas Mavericks were unrecognizable in Thursday’s lopsided 133-94 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves . They didn’t look like the team that won seven of their first 11 games of the season. They were outmuscled inside the paint, outhustled on the glass and turned the ball over throughout the game. Perhaps most importantly, their stars were outperformed. Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg , who scored a season-low in points, attributed their worst loss of the season to their mentality. “Our preparation could’ve been a lot better tonight,” Flagg told The Dallas Morning News . “We came out the gates with just not a good mentality, not a good mindset. I thought we got out of our identity tonight and that led to a lot of disconnected plays as a whole. Flagg went a step further with his analysis of the defeat, which gave him a flashback of his rookie season. “Honestly, it gave me a little reminder of last year, being disconnected,” Flagg told The News . “And it’s contagious. When one person does it, it happens to everybody.” The Mavericks shot a season-low 32% from the field, which could be attributed to Minnesota’s top-ranked defense. After coming off a 43-point performance on Monday , Flagg scored 12 points with seven rebounds. He made five of his 12 shot attempts, but the Timberwolves made it difficult for Flagg and Kyrie Irving to find any comfort offensively. Irving also finished with a season-low in points (10) and had a game-worst minus-36 rating in nearly 27 minutes. Together, Flagg and Irving combined for 22 points, which also marked a season-low for the Mavericks’ dynamic duo. Dallas coach Dusty May said the Timberwolves trapped his stars with defenders well before they could even cross midcourt. And when they didn’t, Flagg and Irving weren’t able to receive clean catches because of Minnesota’s physicality. “We weren’t able to leverage that attention to generate anything else offensively,” May said. With Flagg and Irving limited, there was a ripple effect throughout the team. Dallas was led by Zaccharie Risacher , who made four of his eight 3-point attempts and showed signs that he could regain his shooting stroke from the last two seasons. Naji Marshall added 13 points with four rebounds. “We just gotta lock in as a team before we take that next step,” Marshall said. “Gotta bring it every night because we haven’t done nothing yet. Feels good to get better from last season and win some games early, but we still gotta lock in every day and bring that energy.” Dallas would benefit from Irving returning to his All-Star form for its challenging back-to-back against Cleveland and Boston, but it is unclear if he will play in both games.
